rule: A 'record' claim must state the peak it beats and its date (e.g. 2026 high of $126.41 on Apr 30). Check it against the node's own facts.
Utilities trade on rates and AI power demand, not oil. Check the period and do not call them an oil winner.
Risk parity means equalizing risk contribution across asset classes. It is not a word for concentration risk.
Sector and breadth claims must name the period. September and October 2026 had opposite leadership.

An AI-funding claim must reflect the latest financing events up to meta.asOf. Check the week's hyperscaler bond deals, stock offerings, AI IPO filings and lease financing (on Oct 26, 2026 Meta launched a ~$35B stock offering and Anthropic filed its S-1 for an IPO of up to $100B; both were first left out. SpaceX's $40B GPU debt deal and Musk's warning that debt markets have shut for neoclouds, Oct 25-26, were then left out) and whether the chain's funding channel (bonds vs equity) still holds.
Weekly sector returns differ by proxy (XLK vs S&P 500 IT index). Name the proxy and use one consistently.

rule: A chain that asserts a market regime (bonds not hedging, demand doubt) must be re-tested against the latest week. Check the most recent big equity down days: if Treasuries rallied, or if the latest move had a different cause than the chain's edges, the chain must be rewritten.

A status claim (shut, closed) must match every source on the node for today's date. Lloyd's List and Trading Economics reported Hormuz traffic recovering in October while Reuters said 'largely shut'; disagreement must be stated.
Small caps are not equal weight. The 'Equal vs cap weight' node and any equal-weight conclusion need an equal-weight proxy (RSP or S&P 500 Equal Weight), named.

A move a script or fact attributes to a cause must have that cause in its source. Open the source: if it names several causes (the SOX's eight-day losing run to Oct 16 was put down to oil, interest rates and doubts that AI spending will pay off), do not credit the move to one chain edge alone.

A clause added to a sourced fact or script (a 'first reported' date, an actor's interest or rivalry) must be stated by one of that fact's own cited sources. A review record is not a source: if a fix uses something a reviewer found (in review 2026-10-27-004, the FT's Oct 6 report and SpaceX's compute business), add that source to `sources` and cite it.
